item.title: TCC vs chibicc vs cproc in 2026: Which Tiny C Compiler Should You Actually Use?
item.description: Every C developer has felt it: you change one line, and the build system grinds for ninety seconds to reprocess a dependency graph you have not touched since Tuesday. Full toolchains like GCC and Clang are engineering marvels, but they are also enormous — hundreds of megabytes of binaries carrying decades of optimization passes you did not ask for on an edit-compile-run loop.
